plava: [ plava (plu) + ṇa. Plu-gatiyaṃ. Nīti, dhā. 209. ] (pu) CL=7 (1) Someone or something is floating or appearing on the surface. (2) Someone or something is going quickly. (2) A boat, raft, or ship. (4) jumping up (Ti) (5) That which is floating in the water stream. (6) A floating object.
plavakāla: [ plava + kāla ]  CL=1 A period of floating in the water stream.
plavamāna: [ plava (plu) + māna ] (ti) CL=7 One who floats in the water.
plavanta: [ plava (plu) + anta ] (ti) CL=7 One who floats in the water.
plavati: [ plava (plu) + a + ti ] (kri) CL=7 (1) He floats and flows in the water. (2) He is obvious. (3) He is unrestrained. (4) He runs. (5) He jumps. (6) He swims.
plavattha: [ plava + attha ] (pu) CL=7 The benefit of going quickly.
plavaṅga: [ plava (plu) + gamu + kvi ] (pu) CL=7 A monkey.
plavaṅgama: [ plava (plu) + gamu + a ] (pu) CL=7 A monkey.
plavitabba: [ plava (plu) + tabba ] (ti) CL=7 One who is unrestrained or indignity.
pluta: [ plava (plu) + ta. Pa + ru + ta ]  CL=9 (M) (1) Plut, Pluta. (The vowel- letter which has a reciting period of three matrās or more than the three-matrās. There is no separate enumeration of letters such as consonants, long vowels. It is the letter which is recited in a period of three or more matrās having exceeded the reciting period of even short and long letters.  That Paluta voice is known when calling to a distance, when singing and when crying meloliously. See the extensive explanation in (Thabyaykan, Sya, 1. 45-6). (of a horse) moving swiftly in harmony.
